answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the economy enforces cryptographic stake burning where registering the n-th identity requires burning tokens scaling superlinearly as O(n^2). This steep cost creates a financial mesa that attackers cannot scale, making coordinated mass validation economically unviable. Just as an orchard requires bounded root systems to cultivate value and wild yarrow thrives in distinct clusters, identity verification demands quadratic capital friction to prevent duplicate entities from diluting network governance.
